title: Opaque session handoff protocol and circuited load-shedding for hosted-edge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement an opaque, minimal-state session handoff protocol for hosted API edge pairs to enable active-active traffic shifting with strong stream coherence guarantees, combined with a circuited load-shedding strategy that enforces SLOs during region degradation. Motivation: current edge failover approaches either drop in-flight streams or rely on heavyweight KV replication that increases tail latency. We need a solution that: 1) preserves stream/session continuity for chat/streaming API customers where possible, 2) provides deterministic, measurable SLO behavior under partial regional failure, and 3) integrates with existing circuit-breaker and autoscaling primitives to shed load before violating latency/availability SLOs. Scope: protocol spec (handshake + opaque token exchange), gateway operator changes (traffic shift controller), session-aware backpressure hooks for streaming proxies, circuit-breaker policy templates, telemetry/dashboarding, and canary rollout plan. Non-goals: global KV state replication for full session replication (we only require minimal metadata + rehydration tokens), changes to runtime model checkpointing. Design notes: - Opaque token: short-lived, signed token that encodes minimal session resume metadata (session id, last committed kv checkpoint pointer, model variant, region affinity tag, checksum). Token size target <= 512 bytes. - Handoff handshake: three-phase where source gateway issues token + final KV delta, destination gateway validates token and uses prefix cache rehydration; if validation fails, fallback to per-request transparent retry to origin model with downgrade notice. - Circuited load-shedding: integrate a new edge policy layer that opens a circuit per-route when tail latency or error-rate exceeds route-specific SLO windows (1m, 5m). When open, controller enacts probabilistic shed + degrade-to-fast-variant rules (e.g., smaller model or quantized variant) and exposes informative 503 with retry-after and resume token headers for stream clients. - SLOs & observability: define SLO burn-rate alerts (0.5, 1, 3.0) and dashboard: per-region latency P95/P99, stream resume success rate, token validation failures, shed-rate, and fallback cost delta. - Telemetry hooks: add token lifecycle counters, handshake latency histograms, and a resume success trace that joins origin and destination request ids. Implementation plan: - Gateway: add token encoder/decoder and handshake flow (proxy changes) - Controller: traffic-shift operator support for atomic shift+quarantine windows - Runtime: small API to export session prefix state for one-time rehydrate - Console: add SLO dashboard and runbook links - Tests: unit, integration with streaming client simulator, chaos tests with regional partitioning Rollout: staged canary in single region pair -> cross-region canary with synthetic traffic -> enable for region pairs with conservative shed thresholds -> gradual relaxation. Success criteria: stream resume success >= 90% for sessions <= 30s tail length during normal load; no SLO breaches in non-degraded regions; controlled shed rate < 2% during degradations. Dependencies: design review from Security (token signing key), runtime team to expose rehydrate API, and Console to add dashboard panels.

2026-03-01 - Design review (pm + eng): Meeting notes: choose probabilistic shed before fallback to avoid simultaneous retries; agreed thresholds: start shed at route P95 > 350ms or 5xx rate > 0.8% over 1m. Trade-offs: more aggressive shed reduces resume success but preserves global SLOs. Action: add per-customer override via dedicated flags for enterprise customers.
